review_notes:
I read the whole file. It defines one predicate, `IsHomogeneousElem J r e`, meaning `r` is the class of a degree-`e` form in `MvPolynomial (Fin n) K ⧸ J`. It also has four closure lemmas for it.

Mathlib's closest concept is `SetLike.IsHomogeneousElem 𝒜 x`, which means `∃ i, x ∈ 𝒜 i`. It is built on a `GradedRing 𝒜` structure and used in `Mathlib/RingTheory/GradedAlgebra/Homogeneous/Ideal.lean`. I grepped Mathlib for a graded-ring or homogeneous-ideal structure on quotients and found none at this commit. So the quotient `MvPolynomial ⧸ J` has no `GradedRing` instance to build on.

The file's predicate is also different. It carries an explicit degree `e` as an argument and works for any ideal `J`, not only a homogeneous one. A reuse of `SetLike.IsHomogeneousElem` would need a quotient grading that does not exist.

An alternative is membership in `Submodule.map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K J) (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) K e)`. That is a different representation of the same predicate, and it would not remove any API. The predicate is used in `FreeFiber.lean`, `GradedNorm.lean` and `DegreeUpper.lean`, and those uses give no sign of conversion friction or duplicated API. I could not show a concrete cost of the kind the rubric requires, so I abstain.

The remaining uncertainty is whether a future Mathlib quotient grading would replace this. That does not apply to the pinned commit.
